Royal Bank Of Scotland Group Plc Lowered Apple (AAPL) Position as Valuation Declined; As Exxon Mobil (XOM) Share Value Declined, Synovus Financial Has Upped Position 
April 16, 2018 - By Stephen Andrade 
Royal Bank Of Scotland Group Plc decreased its stake in Apple Inc (AAPL) by 20.34% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Royal Bank Of Scotland Group Plc sold 13,753 shares as the company’s stock declined 3.81% with the market. The institutional investor held 53,863 shares of the computer manufacturing company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $9.12 million, down from 67,616 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Royal Bank Of Scotland Group Plc who had been investing in Apple Inc for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $892.77 billion market cap company. The stock increased 0.70% or $1.22 during the last trading session, reaching $175.95. About 13.27M shares traded. Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) has risen 19.49% since April 16, 2017 and is uptrending. It has outperformed by 7.94% the S&P500. 
Synovus Financial Corp increased its stake in Exxon Mobil Corp (XOM) by 1.83% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Synovus Financial Corp bought 6,801 shares as the company’s stock declined 12.23% with the market. The institutional investor held 378,942 shares of the integrated oil company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $31.67 million, up from 372,141 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Exxon Mobil Corporation (NYSE:XOM) has declined 9.29% since April 16, 2017 and is downtrending. It has underperformed by 20.84% the S&P500. 
Analysts await Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) to report earnings on May, 1. They expect $2.71 earnings per share, up 29.05% or $0.61 from last year’s $2.1 per share. After $3.89 actual earnings per share reported by Apple Inc. for the previous quarter, Wall Street now forecasts -30.33% negative EPS growth.
